audit.whatIsWrong: The page told a reader that Azir dominates this lane — content win[] and the packet chart both give Azir six of seven stages, and the difficulty was set to EVEN at 5.5/10 — while Azir wins 43.37% of 814 games. packet.defects flags the chart contradiction directly. The full layer meanwhile read 'Skill' on rows 0-4, so the two layers also disagreed on five rows.
audit.why: 43.37% over 814 games is a losing lane, not a dominant one. Nothing in either kit supports Azir owning levels 1-4: Pick a Card is a flat 6s auto-reset at every rank, Wild Cards is 6s at rank 1, and Stacked Deck adds damage every fourth attack, so his early trade pattern never goes on cooldown the way the text implied.
audit.corrected: Chart resolved to the full layer's reading rather than the packet's: content win[0..3] Azir -> Skill with whys[0..3] rewritten, and full phases[4].side Skill -> Twisted Fate with its why rewritten, matching content win[4] which already said Twisted Fate. Rows 5 and 6 already agreed on Azir. diff EVEN -> TRICKY, diffRating 5.5/10 -> 7/10, carryRating 6/10 -> 7/10, tone to the TRICKY colour, with breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t updated to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text named 'Shard of True Ice' as Azir's likely first item, and the itemization section elsewhere says Nashor's Tooth. spikes[1].text described Destiny without its cooldown or its reveal.
audit.why: Defect catalogue item 7 — name the real item or drop the clause. Enemy kit R Destiny: 170/140/110, 5500 range, 'revealing all enemy champions and enabling the use of Gate, which teleports Twisted Fate to any target location in 1.5 seconds'.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text now names Nashor's Tooth as the spike; spikes[1].text carries the 170s cooldown, the global reveal and the 1.5s Gate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three factual problems. (a) content.early said 'his Pick a Card (W) has a long cooldown at low levels' — it is a flat 6s at every rank. (b) spikes[0].text said Azir's soldiers out-range Wild Cards — Wild Cards is a 10000-range skillshot. (c) wants.foe[0] read 'Land Gold Card (blue stun card)', which contradicts the page's own gold-is-the-stun convention used everywhere else. Stacked Deck was never mentioned anywhere despite being real lane damage.
audit.why: Enemy kit W Pick a Card: cd 6, 200 range, autoReset flag. Q Wild Cards: 6/5.75/5.5/5.25/5, range 10000, projectile, three cards. E Stacked Deck: 'Every 4 attacks, Twisted Fate deals bonus damage. In addition, his Attack Speed is increased.'
audit.corrected: content.early rewritten around the flat 6s and the three-card fan; spikes[0].text now says Wild Cards is a skillshot to sidestep rather than something you out-range; the contradictory parenthetical is gone; Stacked Deck now appears in tradeBad and whys[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most useful tell in this matchup was absent: Pick a Card resets his auto-attack, so the wind-up animation — not the card cast — is the cue to step back.
audit.why: missingInteractions key 21, rule autoreset-burst-tell, matching the autoReset flag on the W.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and tradeBad.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string pasted verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string pasted verbatim, neither answering its title. dontsFull[1].d quoted nineteen seconds for Shifting Sands; rank 1 is 22s. wants.you[1] claimed Shifting Sands can 'interrupt' his all-in.
audit.why: Defect catalogue items 2 and 6. Owner kit E is a shielded dash with no interrupt or displacement in Riot's text.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to their titles, 22s used, and wants.you[1] now only claims the dash-out that the kit supports.

edits.before: You out-scale his early poke immediately — TF's Wild Cards do modest damage and his Pick a Card (W) has a long cooldown at low levels, so you can Conquering Sands (Q) soldiers to zone him off the wave without much risk. He has no way to punish your E dash-ins pre-6, and his only real threat is a lucky Gold Card, which you can dodge by never standing still in soldier range.
edits.after: The early lane is closer than it looks — Pick a Card is a flat 6s at every rank and it resets his auto, so his card is never really down, and Wild Cards throws three cards on a 6s cooldown for 60 to 100 mana. Zone him off the wave with Conquering Sands (Q) soldiers, keep moving so the fan of cards clips one and not three, and never be standing still when he winds up.

notes: Chart judgement call, flagged deliberately: here the packet chart and the content layer AGREED with each other (Azir 6 of 7 stages) and both contradicted a 43.37% win rate over 814 games — packet.defects says so itself. Rather than copy that into the full layer, I moved the content early rows to 'Skill', which is what the full layer already said, so the two layers now agree AND the page stops claiming Azir dominates a lane he loses. Row 4 moved the other way: full Skill -> Twisted Fate to match content and the packet. Rows 5-6 already agreed. That also drove the difficulty edits (EVEN 5.5/10 -> TRICKY 7/10). If the user disagrees with re-rating the lane, the enum edits are the four to revert; the prose edits stand on their own. I did NOT assert which card colour does what beyond the page's own established gold-is-the-stun convention — Riot's Pick a Card text describes no colours at all, so the blue/red/gold specifics are not sourceable from the kit, and I removed the self-contradicting '(blue stun card)' rather than replacing it with a claim I cannot cite.
